stops.title: City of Delano - Presidents & Mayors
stops.summary: For 150 years, Delano’s story has been shaped not only by the events that changed the community, but by the people who stepped forward to lead it. From the village presidents of its earliest days to the mayors of the modern city, each generation faced its own challenges and made decisions that helped build the Delano we know today. Streets were laid out, wells dug, lights turned on, water and sewer systems built, parks established, and public buildings raised as a small Minnesota village steadily grew into a thriving city. The stories of Delano’s mayors and village presidents offer a glimpse at that journey—and at the local leaders whose service, vision, and everyday decisions helped guide the community through 150 years of change.
stops.name: City Hall

stops.title: Delano Community Development Corporation
stops.subtitle: EST. 1967
stops.summary: In 1967, a group of Delano entrepreneurs and business leaders came together with a shared goal: to bring jobs, industry, and new opportunities to their community. They formed the Delano Community Development Corporation (DCDC), combining private investment, local leadership, and innovative development tools to help shape Delano’s future. Their efforts contributed to projects ranging from industrial development and new businesses to housing for the community’s seniors, leaving an impact that continued long after the organization disbanded in 1980. The story of the DCDC is a remarkable example of what can happen when local citizens invest not only in their businesses, but in the future of their hometown.
stops.name: Delano Community Development Corporation

stops.title: Delano - Franklin Township Area Historical Society
stops.subtitle: Est. 1999
stops.summary: Founded in 1999, the Delano Franklin Township Area Historical Society , (DFTAHS) is dedicated to preserving the artifacts, stories, and historical record of Delano and Franklin Township, with a mission to “preserve the past, enrich the present, and secure the future.” After years without a permanent home, the Society established the historic former Delano City Hall as the Delano Franklin Heritage Center and became an active part of community life through Heritage Festivals, workshops, lectures, exhibits, and educational programs. The Heritage Center later became the heart of the Spirit of Community Trail , helping visitors discover the people, businesses, and buildings that shaped Delano. Although water damage during construction forced the museum to close for renovation, the Society continues its work throughout the community, with a grand reopening of the restored Heritage Center targeted for 2027.
stops.name: Delano Franklin Township Area Historical Society

stops.title: Delano Loretto Area United Way
stops.summary: For generations, the Delano area has answered the needs of its neighbors with generosity and a strong spirit of community. What began with local business leaders and citizens joining together after World War II eventually grew into the Delano–Loretto Area United Way, part of a nationwide tradition of community-based giving. Through door-to-door campaigns, volunteer leadership, annual fundraising drives, and partnerships with local organizations, the effort has evolved along with the communities it serves. From supporting health and human-service organizations to responding to local families in need and unexpected crises, the story of the Delano–Loretto Area United Way reflects an enduring tradition: neighbors coming together to help neighbors and strengthen their community.
stops.name: Delano Loretto Area United Way

stops.title: Delano Public Schools
stops.summary: The 1928 Delano School building stands as a lasting reminder of the community’s long commitment to education. Built at the corner of Elm Avenue and 2nd Street after fire damaged the earlier high school, the new building brought Delano’s grade and high school students together under one roof and was considered one of the finest and best-equipped schools in the area. Its modern gymnasium-auditorium, library, science laboratory, and industrial arts and home economics departments reflected a new era in education. As Delano grew and new schools were built, the building continued to adapt—first serving younger grades and later becoming home to Community Education and other community programs. Nearly a century after it opened, the 1928 school remains an important part of Delano’s educational and community history.
stops.name: Delano Schools

stops.title: Funeral Services
stops.summary: Funeral customs in Delano have changed greatly since the community’s earliest days, when families prepared and cared for their loved ones at home and local carpenters often supplied the coffins. By the late 1800s and early 1900s, undertaking and embalming had become established professions, with funeral parlors gradually replacing services held in family homes. Minnesota’s first licensed woman embalmer, Mrs. Mattie Rader , was one of Delano’s early undertakers. Including Walter M. Tautges and later the Boyce Funeral Service, they provided generations of families with care during times of loss. The history of funeral services in Delano reflects not only changing customs and professions, but also the enduring role of local people and businesses in caring for their neighbors during some of life’s most difficult moments.
stops.name: Funeral Services

stops.title: Fire Department
stops.subtitle: Founded 1874
stops.summary: The Delano Fire Department traces its beginnings to August 1, 1876, when local residents organized the Delano Hook and Ladder Company No. 1. Over the following decades, the department grew from volunteers using hand-operated equipment into an organized community fire service with engines, hose and ladder crews, rural fire trucks, tankers, and modern equipment. Its firefighters responded to many of Delano’s most memorable disasters, including fires that destroyed schools, mills, the Delano Elevator, the Riverside Inn/American Legion Club during the 1965 flood, and the Delano Theater. The department received a new station on Second Street in 1972 and moved into another new fire station there in 2002. Today, the Firefighters Memorial outside the station, featuring Delano’s original fire bell, honors generations of firefighters whose service and dedication have protected the community for well over a century.
stops.name: Fire Department

stops.title: Leiter’s Livery and Auto
stops.address: SE corner of Bridge Ave. and 2nd St.
stops.summary: The corner of Bridge and Second streets tells a remarkable story of Delano’s changing transportation, business, and community life. From schoolhouse and livery barn to automobile garage, factory, civic center, and commercial corner, this site reflects more than a century of change in the heart of Delano.
stops.name: Leiter Livery and Auto

stops.title: Sesquicentennial
stops.subtitle: Delano 150th · 1876-2026
stops.summary: Delano was founded in 1876 along the banks of the Crow River. What started as a small river town has grown into the community you're standing in today, built by generations who showed up for each other. In 2026, Delano celebrated 150 years the way this town does everything: together. The celebration kicked off with a "150 Ways to Celebrate" campaign, giving the town 150 reasons to get involved throughout the year.
stops.name: Sesquicentennial

stops.title: Delano Village Hall
stops.subtitle: Built in 1988
stops.summary: Built in 1888, Delano’s Village Hall quickly became much more than the place where local government conducted its business—it became the heart of community life. The building housed village offices, the fire department, and even a jail, while its upstairs hall welcomed dances, school graduations, basketball games, church dinners, weddings, funerals, and theatrical performances. A stage and dressing rooms were added as entertainment flourished, followed by the familiar tower and fire bell in 1896 and jail cells in 1905. Over the years, the building also provided space for the public library and local elections. Through generations of meetings, celebrations, public service, and everyday gatherings, Delano’s historic City Hall has played a central role in the civic and social life of the community.
stops.name: Old Village Hall

stops.title: Barbers
stops.summary: Barber shops have been a familiar part of Delano’s business community since the town’s earliest years. By 1881, Reynold M. Bohn was serving local customers, and over the decades barbers including Charles Parnell, Beverly C. Yancey, the Bock brothers, Leslie Krumm, and others operated shops along River Street, Franklin Avenue, and Bridge Avenue. Among the longest-lasting traditions was the Stein family’s barbering business: Armand Stein began working in a barber shop as a boy in 1912, eventually opening his own shop, and his son Fran joined the profession in 1967. When Stein’s Barber Shop moved to Bridge Avenue in 2006, historic fixtures—including an 1800s backbar, 1917 barber chairs, and a hand-cranked barber pole—went with it, preserving a tangible connection to more than a century of Delano barbering history.
stops.name: Barbers

stops.title: Bakeries
stops.summary: Bakeries have been a familiar part of Delano’s business community for well over a century. One of the earliest was operated by Napoleon Hamel , who moved to Delano in 1902 and became known for a modern, well-equipped bakery offering breads, cakes, pies, pastries, and other baked goods, some of which were shipped to neighboring communities. He continued in the bakery business until his death in 1927. Other bakeries followed, including the Delano Home Town Bakery, Palm’s Bakery, and Roy and Mrs. Hanson’s bakery, which by 1946 was Delano’s only retail bakery. Perhaps the best remembered was the Delano Bakery , opened by Kerney and Genevieve Jacobson in 1948. For nearly 40 years, the couple produced countless loaves of bread, hundreds of thousands of doughnuts, and thousands of decorated cakes, building a loyal following that extended well beyond Delano. The original bakery closed in 1988, but the Delano Bakery name continued in a new location—almost on the same site where Napoleon Hamel had operated his bakery generations earlier.
stops.name: Bakeries

stops.title: Beck Building
stops.subtitle: Built 1912
stops.summary: The Beck Building at 136 Bridge Avenue E. , built by John M. Beck in 1912 next to Delano’s original City Hall, has housed an unusually diverse collection of businesses during its more than century-long history. Beck, a music teacher and director of the Delano Band, originally used the building for his music and stationery business, while his daughter Clotildis “Claudia” Beck operated a photography studio there and created an important visual record of early Delano. Later occupants included the Delano Granite and Marble Works, several bakeries, the Red Owl grocery store, Ditty Plumbing and Heating, and the Delano Family Dental Clinic. Cutting Edge Construction moved into the historic building in 2005, and portions of the early construction added by monument maker Bert Gilmer can still be seen at the rear. In 2026, the storefront was occupied by Western Creations , continuing the Beck Building’s long tradition of adapting to the changing businesses of downtown Delano.
stops.name: Beck Building

stops.title: Brick Block on Bridge
stops.summary: Built in 1905 on Bridge Avenue , Delano’s Brick Block Building was an ambitious two-story brick commercial building created by Olof Peterson, Louis and Henry Bock, and John L. Stein. Its 100-foot frontage was divided among Peterson’s shoe store, Stein’s business, and a large center section intended for a department store. Before construction was even complete, the center became a gathering place for plays, dances, and community events and later housed businesses and institutions ranging from Kelly & Murray’s department store and the Delano Café to the post office, Picus clothing store, and Rainbow Inn. Over the decades, other portions of the block were home to Heinen Hardware, the Comet Theater, Boyce Funeral Home, Jack’s Food Guild, and the Coast-to-Coast Store, illustrating the building’s central role in generations of Delano commerce and community life. By 2019, the historic building had entered another chapter with The Refoundry and the newly remodeled Jerome Event Center , continuing the Brick Block’s more than century-long presence in downtown Delano.
stops.name: Brick Block on Bridge

stops.title: East Brick Block on Bridge
stops.subtitle: Built 1905
stops.summary: The east end of Delano’s Brick Block at 137 Bridge Avenue E. has served the community through more than a century of changing businesses. Built in 1905 by Olof Peterson in partnership with Henry and Louis Bock and John L. Stein, the property’s early history was connected to Peterson’s shoe store and later to several furniture businesses. In 1933, William Heinen moved his hardware store into the building, where Heinen Hardware remained for 58 years , until 1991. The building later housed Kevin Linquist’s custom framing shop, and its upstairs apartment even appeared as a filming location in the 1998 movie A Simple Plan . More recent occupants have included Delano Floral and Gifts and The Refoundry. After another sale and the naming of the building as the Delano Brick Block , The Vintage Storyteller opened there in May 2026 , continuing the building’s long tradition as a downtown Delano business location.
stops.name: East Brick Block on Bridge

stops.title: Eppel Building
stops.subtitle: Moved to current location in 1871
stops.summary: The Eppel Building at 100 Bridge Avenue E. , at the corner of Bridge Avenue and River Street, is one of Delano’s oldest surviving commercial landmarks. Its history reaches back to 1871 , when Charles Eppel moved the building from south of the railroad tracks to its present location and opened a mercantile store selling dry goods and groceries along with a saloon. The building had also been the Eppel family home, where the first Catholic Mass in the community was celebrated by a missionary priest. Over the years, additions were made and the property housed a harness shop and an early restaurant operated by Charles’s son Leo. During much of the 20th century, the building became closely associated with Curley’s Men’s Clothing Store , later operated by Marshall Dainsberg and then Carroll Lundeen. Since the clothing store closed, numerous businesses have occupied the building, including Linnea’s Ice Cream Parlor, Curves for Women, Cyber Geeks, Bridge House Coffee & Café and Nature Nook Cafe and Wine Bar. Although its exterior has been extensively remodeled, the building retains its original form and remains recognizable as the structure Charles Eppel moved to this prominent downtown corner more than 150 years ago.
stops.name: Eppel Building

stops.title: Hollywood in Delano & Local Talent
stops.summary: Hollywood invaded Delano in 1998 as the film, “A Simple Plan,” starring Billy Bob Thornton, Bill Paxton, Bridget Fonda, and Laura Dern, was shot in and around the village. Filming was set to begin January 2, but due to a lack of snow the crew was forced to go to Ashland, Wisconsin to film exterior scenes. Parts of the film were also shot in Camp Ihduhapi in Loretto, and at the Moravian church near Victoria, MN. There were about 65 small Midwestern towns that were being considered as locations for the film, but Delano’s proximity to the Twin Cities helped its being chosen as the location.
stops.name: Hollywood in Delano

stops.title: Lebovsky Building
stops.summary: The Lebovsky Building at 141 Bridge Avenue E. has been part of Delano’s commercial history since at least 1894, when Olof Peterson operated a boot and shoe store there. Over the following decades, the building housed an assortment of businesses, including the Columbia Clothing Store, shoe and clothing stores operated by the Berlin family and others, a Marshall-Wells associate store, and William Heinen’s hardware business. In 1940, Lebovsky’s Store , a family business founded by Thomas S. Lebovsky on River Street in 1906, moved to the Bridge Street location. The Lebovsky family continued the store for more than four decades, making it a familiar fixture in downtown Delano until it closed in 1984. Since then, the building has been home to Calico Cat Fabrics, the Crow River News, Dwayne’s Games, and Bridge Avenue Ceramics. In 1994, Joe McDonald moved his photography business into the building, beginning another long chapter in the history of this enduring downtown storefront.
stops.name: Lebovsky Building

stops.title: Longosh Building
stops.subtitle: Built in 1906
stops.summary: Built in 1904 by bricklayer and stonemason John Longosh, the Longosh Building has been part of Delano’s Bridge Avenue streetscape for more than 120 years. Longosh, a German immigrant who arrived in Delano in the 1870s, constructed the two-story brick building with commercial space below and living quarters above. The Longosh Building SoCT Over the decades, the building housed an assortment of businesses, including a saloon, barber shop, Curley’s clothing store, a harness and leather shop, and Bill’s Shoe Repair. The Longosh Building SoCT Its long history reflects the changing businesses and everyday life of downtown Delano. Today, in 2026, the historic building continues its commercial role as the home of Vintage on Bridge and the Book Nook .
stops.name: Longosh Building

stops.title: State Bank of Delano Building
stops.subtitle: Built 1908
stops.summary: 1908: The State Bank of Delano was incorporated. 1910: The State Bank of Delano and the Wright County Bank was consolidated.
stops.name: State Bank of Delano

stops.title: West Brick Block on Bridge
stops.subtitle: Built 1905
stops.summary: The west end of Delano’s Brick Block has been home to a remarkable variety of businesses and community services since the building was constructed in 1905. J. L. Stein developed this portion of the block on the site of an old blacksmith shop, with the Northwestern Telephone Company occupying rooms upstairs soon afterward. Over the following decades, the building housed a men’s clothing store, the Delano Variety Store, a furniture business, the Comet Theater, and Dr. F. R. Shanahan’s dental practice. By the 1930s it was home to the Boyce Funeral Home, and in 1941 Jack Schumacher purchased the property, remodeled the storefront, and moved his Jack Sprat grocery store there. The business later became Jack’s Food Guild , remaining until Schumacher’s retirement in the mid-1970s. The space eventually became part of Coast to Coast Hardware and today forms part of the Jerome Event Center , continuing the Brick Block’s long role in Delano’s downtown commercial life.
stops.name: West Brick Block on Bridge

stops.title: Beauty Shops
stops.summary: Delano’s beauty shops emerged in the late 1920s as changing fashions, especially women “bobbing” their hair, created a new demand for professional hairstyling. Martha Lindsley advertised a beauty shop in her home in 1926, and by the 1930s more Delano women were independently owning and operating their own shops. Over the decades, businesses such as the Mella-Dor Beauty Box, Kitty’s Beauty Shop, the Bridge Corner Barber and Beauty Shop, and others became fixtures of the community. Margaret “Kitty” Kittock’s business survived the 1971 Delano Theater fire and eventually became the Downtown Beauty Shop, which Pat Schroeder operated until her retirement in 2025. Together, these shops and the women who operated them reflect nearly a century of changing hairstyles, entrepreneurship, and small-town life in Delano.
stops.name: Beauty Shops

stops.title: Big Wood Garden Club
stops.subtitle: EST. 2002
stops.summary: Founded in 2002 as part of the Delano Dream Team’s effort to beautify Historic Downtown Delano, the Big Woods Garden Club brought together people who shared a love of gardening and a desire to improve their community. Through plant sales, garden tours, educational programs, and countless hours of volunteer work, members created and maintained community gardens, landscaped the Delano Public Library, supported local organizations, cared for area roadsides, and helped beautify downtown Delano. When River Front Park was established following the installation of the downtown flood walls in 2017, the club once again contributed both plants and helping hands to beautify River Street. They have recently established garden to accent some of the sculptures installed in the Delano Sculpture Park. Over the years, the Big Woods Garden Club combined community service, gardening education, friendship, and plenty of “green thumbs” to leave a lasting mark on Delano and the surrounding area.
stops.name: Big Woods Garden Club

stops.title: Cramer Building
stops.summary: The Cramer Building at 224 River Street N. has been part of Delano’s commercial history since the late 1800s and was long associated with one of the city’s oldest meat markets. Joseph Cramer operated a meat market on River Street as early as 1879, later joined by his son Frank, and by the mid-1880s Cramer was constructing a new brick building at the site. The meat market tradition continued under J. M. Wandok and later Everett LaFave, whose market remained a familiar River Street business for decades. In 1972, nearly a century after Cramer began his business, the building became home to Delano TV and subsequently housed a variety of businesses. Today, the historic storefront is home to LuLu’s Retail Therapy , which opened in January 2020 and offers women’s clothing and accessories, baby items, home décor, and gifts.
stops.name: Cramer Building

stops.title: Delano Chamber of Commerce
stops.subtitle: EST. 1967
stops.summary: The Delano Area Chamber of Commerce traces its beginnings to 1939, when local businessmen organized a Santa Claus Day for Delano children, an effort that grew into a broader movement to promote the community and support local commerce. On June 3, 1941, the group formally organized as a Civic Club dedicated to advancing the interests of local merchants, expanding Delano’s trade area, and encouraging community activities and improvements. In 1953, Articles of Incorporation were adopted and the organization became the Delano Civic and Commerce Club . Through community celebrations, banquets, promotions, and other civic projects, the organization played an important role in bringing Delano’s business community together and supporting the growth and vitality of the city.
stops.name: Delano Chamber of Commerce

stops.title: Delano Granite Works
stops.subtitle: Founded 1917
stops.summary: Founded in 1917 by Bert Gilmer , Delano Granite Works grew from a small monument shop into an internationally significant Delano industry and, by 1944, the world’s largest granite memorial retailer . From its plant along the Crow River, the company expanded dramatically, owning quarries, production facilities, and a sales organization while adopting increasingly sophisticated equipment for cutting, polishing, and finishing stone. It became one of Delano’s largest employers and an important part of the community’s civic and economic life. In 1964, the company expanded beyond monuments into structural granite, supplying stone for projects including the General Mills headquarters . Don Gilmer succeeded his father in leading the company in 1956, and the Granite Works continued operating until its closure in 1984 . Although the former industrial site has since been redeveloped, granite found throughout Delano remains a visible reminder of a company that helped shape the community for nearly seven decades.
stops.name: Delano Granite Works

stops.title: Delano United Diversity Task Force
stops.subtitle: Founded in 2017
stops.summary: Founded in 2017 as Delano United , the Delano United Diversity Task Force (DUDTF) is a grassroots volunteer organization working to make the Delano area a more welcoming and equitable community. Its efforts have included community speakers and book discussions, support for student and parent groups, anti-bullying and equity initiatives, participation in local parades, the weekly On Welcoming newspaper column, and advocacy for affordable housing. More recently, the group has helped research and share the area’s Indigenous history as part of Delano’s Sesquicentennial activities, including contributing information for the commemorative book and connecting the mural project with Dakota cultural resources. Today, DUDTF continues to partner with local organizations and encourage volunteers to help foster inclusion and a sense of welcome for everyone who lives, works, plays, and prays in the Delano community.
stops.name: Delano United Diversity Task Force

stops.title: First National Bank of Delano
stops.subtitle: Built 1908
stops.summary: Built in late 1908 to house the Wright County Bank, the building at 220 River Street North has been a familiar part of downtown Delano for more than a century. By 1910, the bank was settled into its impressive new quarters, which featured oak interior finishes, tile floors, a steel ceiling, electric lighting, and other modern conveniences. The building later became home to First National Bank and, beginning in March 1965, the Delano Post Office. Over the years it has continued to serve the community through a variety of businesses, including a real estate office and photography studio, reflecting the many changes that have shaped Delano’s downtown.
stops.name: First National Bank

stops.title: GP Schaffer Building
stops.subtitle: Built 1897
stops.summary: Built in 1906, the two-story brick building at 248 River Street North has been part of Delano’s downtown story for more than a century. Originally constructed by E. F. Ziebarth and Thomas Lebovsky, it has housed an ever-changing variety of businesses and residents through the decades, surviving changes in ownership, a major fire, and the evolution of downtown Delano itself. Today, following an extensive renovation, the historic building is known as the Whiskey Jar Pud and Eatery and continues its long tradition as a vibrant part of the community.
stops.name: GP Schaffer Building

stops.title: Crow River Floods/Wagon Bridge
stops.summary: The first people to travel the Crow River were the Wahpekute (Shooters Among the Leaves) band of the Oceti Sakowin meaning Seven Council Fires, known as the Great Sioux Nation. In 1853, Wright County was open to white settlement. Trappers, traders, farmers, and shopkeepers began to move into the Big Woods following the Crow River to the area which was to become Delano. Although the river provided transportation, power and recreation, Delano has had a long history of high water, ice dams and flooding. The Crow River Bridges provided a important link between settlements on both sides of the river when the water was not low enough to ford.
stops.name: Wagon Bridge / Crow River Floods

stops.title: Ziebarth/Lebovsky Block
stops.subtitle: Built 1906
stops.summary: Built in 1906, the two-story brick building at 248 River Street North has been part of Delano’s downtown story for more than a century. Originally constructed by E. F. Ziebarth and Thomas Lebovsky, it has housed an ever-changing variety of businesses and residents through the decades, surviving changes in ownership, major floods, and the continuing evolution of downtown Delano.
stops.name: Ziebarth/Lebovsky Block

stops.title: Bernick Building
stops.subtitle: Built 1885
stops.summary: Built in 1885 at 162 River Street North, the Bernick Building has stood at one of Delano’s busiest corners for more than 140 years. The site’s commercial history began in 1869 with John Borsch’s store and saloon, but after the original wooden building was destroyed by fire in 1885, the Bernick family replaced it with the handsome two-story brick building that remains today. Over the decades, the corner became especially well known for its saloons and taverns, including John Stein’s Corner Saloon and, beginning in 1941, the popular Main Bar. In 1956, the building became home to Delano Municipal Liquor, whose on-sale establishment was famously known as “The Zoo.” After the municipal liquor operation moved in 1983, the building served a variety of businesses and today continues its long commercial life as the home of Crow River Studio—preserving a landmark that has witnessed generations of change in downtown Delano.
stops.name: Bernick Building

stops.title: Millinery
stops.summary: At a time when few career opportunities were available to women, millinery offered Delano women a way to build independent businesses and serve the fashionable needs of their community . Among the best known was Rosa “Rosie” Geiger Adler Zabel , who opened her millinery business at about age 19 and operated what became the Zabel Style Shop for more than 50 years. Her shop offered carefully crafted hats decorated with velvet, satin, fur, chiffon, silk, feathers, flowers, ribbons, and other fashionable trims, as well as sewing services for local women. Delano was also home to other women in the millinery trade, including Eva Mulford, Maggie O’Leary, Agnes Fleming Leonard, and Bertha Belt . Their shops provided Delano women with the latest styles while giving these early businesswomen an important and distinctive place in the city’s commercial history.
stops.name: Millinery

stops.title: Rieder Meat Market
stops.subtitle: EST. 1911
stops.summary: For generations, Rieder Meat Market was a beloved fixture of downtown Delano and one of the community’s longest-running family businesses. The site at 150 River Street North had housed a meat market since 1876, and in 1911 Leonard J. Rieder and August Schilling established Rieder & Schilling Meat Market. The present building was constructed in 1920, and after Schilling’s death, the business continued through generations of the Rieder family, becoming known for quality meats, personal service, and strong ties to the community. Both Leonard J. Rieder and his son Laurence served as mayors of Delano, further connecting the family to the city’s history. After 115 years under the Rieder name, the market closed in July 2026 with the retirement of third-generation owner Laurence “Bud” Rieder Jr., bringing to a close a remarkable chapter in Delano’s downtown history.
stops.name: Rieder Meat Market

stops.title: Plattner Building
stops.summary: Since 1892, this building has housed a variety of businesses that reflect Delano’s changing commercial life. It began as John B. Plattner’s General Store , where customers could purchase everything from dry goods and overcoats to boots, hats, furnishings, and notions, promoted through Plattner’s enthusiastic weekly advertisements in the Delano Eagle . In 1913, the building was sold to William Picus , who operated the business until 1920, while Dr. Charles Parker maintained his dental office upstairs. By 1940, Warhol’s Rexall Drug Store occupied the building and featured an impressive 30-foot soda fountain made of Central American primavera wood. The building later became home to Brown Plumbing , and in 1987 began another chapter as Dave’s Town Club , continuing nearly a century of service as a familiar part of Delano’s downtown business district.
stops.name: Plattner Building

stops.title: 120 River Street North
stops.subtitle: Built 1897
stops.summary: Built around 1897, the building at 120 River Street North has served a remarkable variety of Delano businesses for more than a century. One of its earliest occupants was a confectionery, followed by a jewelry store by 1909; in 1925, watchmaker and jeweler Peter Magdzas purchased the business, and Peter’s Jewelry remained there for sixteen years. In 1941, Don Bartlett and Ray Kiefer purchased the building and moved their popular tavern there, followed by Shelly and Sterling Robson, who operated the bar until Delano established its Municipal Liquor Store in 1956. The building later housed the Delano Chiropractic Office, the Perkins and Grinley Law Office, and optometrist Dr. Dale R. Petersen. Continuing its long history as a downtown business location, Delano Floral & Gifts has occupied the building since 2014.
stops.name: 120 River St. N.

stops.title: Borsch Building
stops.subtitle: Built in 1897 · 116 River St. N,
stops.summary: Built in 1897 at 116 River Street North, the John E. Borsch Building has housed more than a century of Delano businesses, beginning with T. B. Rader’s hardware and well supplies and later A. W. Wittman’s drug store. In 1921, Edward W. Keplinger purchased the building and moved his grocery business there, eventually opening Delano’s first Red & White store. After his death, his son Horace “Kep” Keplinger and wife Esther continued the business, expanding its produce operation—especially eggs—into an enterprise that eventually grew into Wrightco. Although the building was gutted by fire in 1932, it was rebuilt and continued serving Delano through a succession of businesses. Today, the historic storefront is home to Mainstreet Boutique, continuing the building’s long tradition as part of Delano’s River Street business district.
stops.name: Borsch Building

stops.title: Post Office
stops.subtitle: Built 1965
stops.summary: Delano’s postal history began in 1858 with the Cassel post office west of present-day Delano. With the arrival of the railroad in 1868, postal service shifted to the new community along the Crow River, which soon took the name Delano in honor of railroad official Francis Roach Delano. Over the following century, the post office moved among several downtown businesses and buildings and was served by a long succession of postmasters, including Delano’s first female postmaster, Miranda Chance, in 1880. Rural free delivery began in 1901, with three routes eventually serving Delano and surrounding communities. In 1926, the post office moved into the former First National Bank building on River Street, where it remained until a new post office was built and dedicated in 1965—the same year Delano experienced its record-breaking flood. The story continues through generations of postmasters and changing postal services, reflecting more than 165 years of Delano’s growth and community life.
stops.name: Post Office

stops.title: Delano Lions
stops.summary: The Delano Lions Club supports the community through local events, fundraising, and infrastructure projects. The Lions Club was organized in Delano in November 1965 with twenty-one members on the original list and several more joining by the charter night, December 9, 1965. The Lions Club was organized to fill the need in Delano for a service club. The organizing members felt that they could contribute to the overall improvement of the Delano community. Over the next several years the Lions sponsored Cub Scouts, bike safety clinics, Tots-to-Teens Talent contests, the Lions Eye Bank, the Christmas lighting contest, and snowmobile races. They furnished playground equipment and a shelter in Central Park, and became instrumental in the 4th of July celebration. The Lions purchased a Rescue truck for the Delano Fire Department and were involved in having Delano join the Great River Regional library system, and in financing the renovation of the library. The Lions built the entryway to the Franklin Township Hall and were founding members of the original Delano Community Development Committee that brought Industrial Louvers (then ACP) to Delano.
stops.name: Delano Lions

stops.title: Delano Boy Scouts Troop 273
stops.summary: Boy Scouts of America got its start in 1910. Eight years later, Delano welcomed Troop 273 (formerly 173). For nearly 100 years, hundreds of scouts from Delano and the surrounding communities have worked to better themselves by giving back their community. In the Fall of 1928, nine young Delano boys started blazing a trail for decades of scouts to follow. Whether it was learning valuable outdoor skills, learning how to be a good citizen, or serving their community; Delano Scouts continue to serve our city with pride.. During times of war and times of peace, Delano Scouts have stood the test of time and remains a strong and active community organization. Delano Scouts are involved in supporting community events including Old Fashioned Christmas, collecting food for the Delano Food Shelf, 4th of July Celebrations and much more. The troop meets most Mondays at the Heritage Center
stops.name: Delano Boy Scouts Troop 273

stops.title: Delano-Loretto Girl Scouts
stops.summary: Girl Scouting in Delano began in the summer of 1931, less than 20 years after the national organization was founded. Early Girl Scouts participated in camping, swimming, canoeing, outdoor cooking, crafts, nature study, community activities and local fundraising. Delano Girl Scouts History After the original troop became inactive, Girl Scouting was reorganized in Delano in 1951 with 29 girls and grew to include Brownie and Intermediate troops. A major change came in 1965 when Delano joined the Greater Minneapolis Girl Scout Council and organized Brownie, Junior, Cadette and Senior levels. Delano Girl Scouts History Generations of local women have served as scouts and leaders, including Maria Logsdon, who contributed at least 20 years of service. Eventually known as the Delano-Loretto Girl Scouts, the organization has carried forward a tradition of friendship, leadership, service and outdoor adventure that began in Delano in 1931. Delano Girl Scouts History Delano Girl Scouts History
stops.name: Delano Loretto Girl Scouts

stops.title: Stein Barber Shop
stops.summary: The Stein family’s barbering legacy in Delano began with Armand Stein , who started at the Bock Barber Shop in 1912 at just eight years old, shining shoes and lathering customers for shaves. Licensed as a barber at only 15, Armand later traveled to California, where he cut the hair of several Hollywood actors before returning to Delano and opening Stein’s Barber Shop in 1932. Armand retired in 1978 after 61 years of barbering, while his son Fran, who joined him in 1967, continued the family tradition. When the historic River Street building was demolished by controlled burn in 2006, Fran moved the shop to Bridge Avenue, preserving its original backbar, 1917 barber chairs, and rare hand-cranked barber pole. He continued barbering until selling the shop in 2025. Together, Armand and Fran Stein provided Delano with an extraordinary 119 years of barbering service spanning two generations .
stops.name: Stein Barber Shop

stops.title: Delano Area Council for Arts and Culture
stops.subtitle: EST. 2009
stops.summary: The mission of the Delano Area Council for Arts and Culture is to empower people to think, work and live creatively through arts and cultural experiences.
stops.name: Delano Area Council for Arts & Culture

stops.title: Delano Original Commercial District
stops.subtitle: Est. 1869
stops.summary: The photo was taken from the point where the railroad bridge crosses River Street. There are fifteen people showing in the picture, seven on the second story of the hotel veranda, one woman, three men, four children, one dog and many, many round-head rocks in the foreground. The first building from the left was built in the winter of 1868-69 by F. B. Nichols, who conducted a general store. The next building, in the center of the picture, was the Avenue House. Miner Ball had moved it in from Greenwood. It was run by J. F. Powers, later became Young’s Hotel in 1871, and eventually was known as the Great Northern Hotel. To the right of the hotel was a general store conducted by Frank Hopkins. The two-story white building on the edge of the clearing was the Chance building.
stops.name: Delano Original Commercial District

stops.title: Grain Elevators
stops.summary: Grain elevators have been central to Delano’s agricultural and commercial life since the community’s earliest days. When the railroad reached Crow River in 1868, plans already called for a 40,000-bushel elevator, and by 1881 the locally organized Delano Elevator Company had constructed its distinctive round elevator, helping make Delano an important regional grain market. The elevator business evolved through different owners and cooperatives, eventually coming under the Styrbicky family, whose Delano Elevator Company expanded into feed grinding and mixing. A devastating fire destroyed the elevator and grinding mill in March 1962, but a modern steel elevator and feed plant was built and opened the following year. The Styrbicky family continued the business until 2011, when Mike “Spike” Persons purchased it and established Spike’s Feed, Seed & Pet Supply, carrying Delano’s grain and feed tradition into a new generation.
stops.name: Grain Elevators

stops.title: Great Northern Hotel
stops.subtitle: Built in 1879 · Railroad Avenue
stops.summary: The Great Northern Hotel was a prominent part of Delano’s early history, serving generations of travelers and salesmen arriving by rail. Its story began in 1868, when Miner Ball moved a small building from the former townsite of Greenwood to Delano and opened it as a hotel. Under James D. Young, it grew into the much larger Young’s Hotel, a three-story landmark capable of accommodating scores of guests and offering a livery stable for travelers continuing to neighboring communities. After operating for a time as the Meister House, John and Magdalena Pfeifer purchased the property in 1901, and in 1902 it became the Great Northern Hotel . Lena Pfeifer continued operating it for decades after her husband’s death. A later fire damaged the third floor, which was subsequently removed, and the building eventually became the Pfeifer Hotel and then an apartment building before being demolished in 1971—ending more than a century of service at this historic Delano site.
stops.name: Great Northern Hotel

stops.title: Delano Library
stops.subtitle: built 1975
stops.summary: The Delano Public Library has served the community from several locations since its beginnings in 1930, reflecting both the library’s growth and Delano’s changing downtown. It began in Brown’s Drug Store before moving to the Village Council Chambers in 1940, and by 1952 had a paid librarian. The library joined the Great River Regional Library system in 1969 and subsequently operated from St. Joseph’s Educational Building and, beginning in 1974, the former fire barn on Bridge Avenue, which was renovated by the Crow River Women’s Club. In 2004, the library moved into the former Delano State Bank site, continuing a long tradition of adapting historic community spaces to provide library service to generations of Delano residents.
stops.name: Delano Library

stops.title: Eagle Building
stops.subtitle: Built 1883
stops.summary: The Delano Eagle Building at 300 Railroad Avenue represents more than a century of Delano’s newspaper and printing history. The story began in 1872 with the Big Woods Citizen , which soon became the Wright County Eagle and, in 1881, the Delano Eagle . In 1883, a two-story building constructed of locally produced red brick became the newspaper’s permanent home and Delano’s first solid brick building. Its second floor, known as Eagle Hall, also served as an early community entertainment space. In addition to publishing the newspaper, the Eagle Printing Company became known for railroad and commercial printing and operated a highly regarded bookbindery. The Eagle Newspaper and Job Printing Office remained at this Railroad Avenue location for more than 100 years, and its three-building complex was listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1979, preserving the legacy of one of Delano’s oldest and most enduring businesses.
stops.name: Eagle Building

stops.title: Independent Order of Odd Fellows
stops.subtitle: EST.1881
stops.summary: Built in 1881 for the C.F. Peters' General Store. The second story served as a hall for the Odd Fellows, Mason, Woodmen, Eastern Star and other lodges.
stops.name: Independent Order of Odd Fellows

stops.title: Lindsley Building
stops.subtitle: Built 1869
stops.summary: The Lindsley Building at 282 Railroad Avenue has been part of Delano’s downtown landscape since 1885, when Joseph Warren Lindsley constructed the handsome two-story brick building to expand his hardware business. Considered one of the finest business blocks in Delano at the time, it featured modern improvements, including an elevator, with the hardware store on the first floor and living quarters above. After leaving the hardware business, Lindsley remodeled the building and opened the Lindsley Hotel in 1909, described as a “thoroughly modern” hostelry. By 1918 it had become known as Packer’s Hotel under James Packer. Although the exact date of its later conversion has not yet been determined, the historic building eventually became apartments and continues to serve as residential housing today.
stops.name: Lindsley Building

stops.title: Lundsten Lumber
stops.subtitle: EST. 1903
stops.summary: Established in 1903 by O.J. Lundsten as the Home Lumber Company and renamed Lundsten Lumber in 1906, the business became one of Delano’s oldest and most enduring family enterprises. Located on Railroad Avenue near the depot, the lumber yard grew into an extensive operation supplying lumber, brick, lime, cement, coal, and other building materials. Management passed from O.J. Lundsten to his nephew Cliff Lundsten and later to Cliff’s son Jim and his wife Ann, while generations of the Lundsten family also played important roles in Delano’s civic and community life. When the family sold the business in 1988, Lundsten Lumber was Delano’s oldest business still under the same family management. The historic building remains in use today as the home of Love INC , preserving a visible connection to more than a century of Delano history.
stops.name: Lundsten Lumber

stops.title: Railroad
stops.subtitle: Arrived 1868
stops.summary: The railroad was central to Delano’s founding and development. When the St. Paul & Pacific Railroad reached the Crow River in 1868, the new settlement grew around its station and depot and was soon named Delano in honor of railroad official F. R. Delano. The Railroad Line The railroad brought passengers, commerce, grain and new businesses, while its bridge across the Crow River and depot became important local landmarks. A new depot was built in 1885, and a new 270-foot railroad bridge followed in 1904, with the bridge undergoing extensive rebuilding in the 1940s. The Railroad Line The Railroad Line The line eventually became part of the Great Northern, Burlington Northern and, today, BNSF Railway. Although Delano’s depot was torn down in 1988, the railroad line and bridge remain enduring reminders of the transportation network that helped create and shape the community. The Railroad Line The Railroad Line
stops.name: The Railroad

stops.title: Wright County Bank Building
stops.subtitle: Build 1885
stops.summary: Timeline: 1868-69 – F.B. Nichols built a store on Railroad Avenue between the current 2nd and 3rd streets. He opened a general store, and was the second postmaster of Delano. 1873 – F. B. Nichols sold the building and stock of goods to Row Brasie. 1880 – Wright County Bank founded by C M. Dittman and C. G. Roosen in building bought from Row Brasie 1882 – Roosen bought out Dittman, and continued the business as a private bank 1884 – Wright County Bank of Delano incorporated, in new building at 204 Railroad Ave. 1893 – Wright County Bank is still located at 204 Railroad Avenue 1910 – Wright County Bank is now located at 220 River Street 1910 – The Wright County Bank and the State Bank of Delano merged, and located in the building at 115 Bridge Avenue E. 2019 – the building at 204 Railroad Avenue is currently used for apartments
stops.name: Wright County Bank

stops.title: American Legion Post #377
stops.summary: The Delano American Legion Post #377 was organized in the spring of 1920. There were forty-one charter members. The first officers of the post were Frank Brunkow, Commander; J. W. Lohmiller, Vice-Commander; Albert McEachern, Post Adjutant; Ury Hanseman, Post Finance Officer; and John Tomnitz, Post Historian. Following a membership drive later that year, membership increased to sixty-one. The purpose of the organization and the reason every ex-serviceman should become a member as stated in 1920 were: 1. Because a loyal American citizen, a veteran of the World War, should earnestly desire to help his country in peace, as well as in war. 2. Being more fortunate than others who have served the United States during the World War, they should desire to help the sick, wounded, disabled and destitute veteran. 3. The comradeship of mutual service forms a band between individuals who served in the World War that cannot be ignored. 4. An organized American Legion is a strong factor is securing the United States against war. 5. To promote and foster patriotism. 6. There is a personal satisfaction in accomplishing good, and there is a feeling of pride in wearing the emblem of an organization that is universally recognized as a power for good in all communities. 7. No class – no rank – just comrades.
stops.name: Delano American Legion

stops.title: Delano Creamery
stops.subtitle: EST. 1895
stops.summary: The Delano Creamery began in 1895 when local banker C. G. Roosen, hoping to improve difficult economic conditions for area farmers, established a creamery after an initial attempt to organize a cooperative drew little support. Through persistent efforts to recruit farmers and arrange milk-hauling routes, the business quickly grew, and in 1898 local farmers purchased the operation and formed the Delano Co-operative Creamery Association. By 1909, the creamery had become one of the area’s leading manufacturing and shipping industries, with much of its product shipped to New York City, and its award-winning butter earned Delano a reputation for quality. By 1915 it served about 220 patrons and received milk from an estimated 1,800 cows, while buttermaker Emil G. Oman was recognized as a national champion. The operation later shifted largely to bottling milk and cream for local and Minneapolis markets. The creamery closed in the 1970s, and after housing other businesses for a time, the building was demolished in 2006; Delano’s sculpture walk now occupies the former site.
stops.name: Delano Creamery

stops.title: Delano Municipal Utilities
stops.subtitle: Built 1932
stops.summary: Delano’s municipal utilities grew alongside the community, beginning with streetlights and a city well in 1879 and expanding after voters approved bonds for electric lights and waterworks in 1894. The original power plant on South River Street used a wood-burning steam engine, while wells and a water tower supplied water for both fire protection and household use. As demand increased, Delano expanded electric service, established 24-hour A.C. service in 1915, built its own distribution system in 1927, and opened a new diesel power plant in 1932—making Delano the only town in Wright County with a municipally owned light and power plant. The system continued to modernize with larger generators, expanded facilities, a new substation, a major water tower in 2002, and a new water treatment plant in 2006. The utility also weathered some of Delano’s most dramatic floods, including the 1965 flood, when a Navy helicopter rescued five men stranded inside the flooded power plant because the Crow River was too dangerous for a boat rescue.
stops.name: Delano Municipal Utilities

stops.title: Hildebrandt Building
stops.subtitle: EST. 1926
stops.summary: The Rockford Woolen Mills Co. – to – Riverside Commons (from The Minneapolis Journal, Tuesday, November 7, 1905) MILLS TO BE MOVED Delano Organizes Company to Secure Rockford Industry DELANO, MINN. – A company has been organized here with a capital stock of $15,000, of which $10,000 is already paid up, for the purpose of moving the machinery of the Rockford Woolen mills to this place. The following officers have been selected: George P. Schaffer, president; J. E. Borsch, vice president; Charles E. Parker, secretary; L.P. Probst, treasurer, The board of directors are: J. E. Borsch, Adam Horsch, A. L. Mealey, M.E. Muckey, E. T. Ziebarth, F. J. Benner and Frank Roban. A site will be selected and the erection of a building commenced at once. The woolen mill will give employment to many, and will make quite an addition to the business of interested of Delano. Should the business of the concern warrant, the mills will be increased to double its present capacity and more stock to cover the expense of building will be sold. This can be easily done, as the $10,000 in shares were sold in less than one day’s work, and many other citizens were still anxious to buy.” (from The Delano Eagle, November 16, 1905) “The site of the woolen mills has been selected – part of the Ed Bock property on the west side. The piece was purchased for a consideration of $1,000. Work on the foundation of the building will be commenced at once and the structure erected as fast as possible so as to get the machinery in place in a few months. Mr. Brenner is anxious to begin work on his next year’s orders and every effort will be made to push the work forward.” (from the Delano Eagle, November 23, 1905) “The foundation for the woolen mills is about completed and the work of erecting the building will be commenced at once. The ground around the site is being graded and put in good shape to allow easy access to the building with teams. The way this enterprise is being carried to completion speaks loud for the business push of those who have taken hold of the industry.” (from The Delano Eagle, December 14, 1905) “A large crew of men are at work on the woolen mill and rushing it rapidly forward. It will not be many days before another steam whistle will announce that the wheels of this industry have been set in motion.” (from The Delano Eagle, January 11, 1906) “F. J. Benner and family arrived last Thursday from points in Wisconsin where they had visited and are now occupying their rooms in the new brick block. Mr. Benner informs us that he will commence this week the work of placing the machinery in the new building, and the work will be pushed forward as rapidly as possible.” (from The Delano Eagle, January 11, 1906) “A meeting of the directors of the Woolen Mill Co. was held last Monday evening and one of the important matters for consideration was the purchasing of an engine, boiler and elevator. Mr. Reichard, representing a Minneapolis firm, was present explaining the qualities of his goods. Several price lists were submitted by different firms and after considerable discussion, Mr. Muckey and Mr. Horsch were appointed a committee to do the purchasing. They will go to the city this week to attend to the matter as the building is now ready for the placing of this part of the equipment.” (from The Delano Eagle, March 22, 1906) AN UP-TO-DATE FACTORY ___________ The Rockford Mills Company is Adding New Machinery and Fitting Up Its Plant in First-Class Shape “In order to be thoroughly up-to-date, the Rockford Woolen Mills Company has purchased several new pieces of machinery which are expected to arrive at any time and which will make their mill one of the most complete in the country. It is the policy of the directors to expend sufficient money to get rid of any handicap that might stand in the way of producing goods at the least possible cost. More money has been expended upon the equipment than was at first thought necessary, but every dollar has been spent with a view to obtaining the best results when operations are commenced. Anybody visiting the mill will readily see that the equipment is first-class in every way and that a permanent and prosperous industry is planned. The market for such goods as the mill will turn out is practically unlimited and the margins of profit are very satisfactory. All that is necessary is to keep the quality of the goods up and to work the factory to its full capacity all the year round, and this can easily be done through the system of steam heating that has been installed. In order to furnish ample working capital and to take advantage of discounts, etc., the directors have decoded to dispose of the remainder of the stock which will no doubt, be readily taken up by local parties. The business integrity and standing of those interested insures an honest and efficient management and the investment will no doubt prove a very profitable and satisfactory one.” (from The Delano Eagle, 19__ _) At the meeting of the stockholders of the woolen mill a bid from the Lundsten Lumber Co. was received in which $3,000 was offered for the concern. By a vote of the stock the bid was accepted but when the impression was allowed to prevail that the company intended tearing the building down and disposing of the machinery a strenuous kick was registered, which was so strong that the bid was withdrawn. This leaves the woolen mill situation as it has been for the past year. There seems to be no solution to the difficulty in the way o getting the mill running again. What the outcome will be is hard to say. The slight indebtedness is liable to eat up all the money invested unless some disposition can be made of the property whereby it will be operated. Should this prove to be the case it is liable to injure any industry which might be brought up for consideration in the future The greatest difficulty seems to lie in the fact that for the past few years like institutions have suffered a loss because of a plethora of woolen goods on the market, which has forced prices down so that the goods cannot be manufactured at a profit and the capital invested has had no return whatever. Another hindrance is that goods have to be sold nearly a year in advance and in this it would be necessary to have a man on the road at a fair salary in order to know just how much would have to be turned out. This of course takes more capital than the stockholders care to put up. But such things have got to be considered in cases of this kind.” (from the Delano Eagle,19__ ) “M. E. Muckey and Oscar Hildebrandt have purchased the woolen mill for a consideration of $12.00 per share, they assuming all the indebtedness, the total consideration being about $3,200. Muckey & Hildebrandt will open a repair shop and automobile garage for the present and will no doubt do a good business, as both are expert mechanics. Later on they intend to add other enterprises to their shop, one of which we hear reported as being a steam laundry. They will dispose of he machinery used in the woolen mill, which will give them ample space for all kinds of work.” (from The Delano Eagle, Milton E Muckey obituary, January 24, 1937) “When Delano business men took over the Rockford woolen mill and moved it to Delano, he installed most of the machinery. Later on he and O. B. Hildebrandt purchased the woolen mill property and started an automobile garage which was the first Ford agency in Wright County. In 1922, Mr. Muckey retired and the agency was transferred to Mr. Hildebrandt, who now handles Chevrolet motor cars and trucks.” (from The Delano Eagle, Oscar Hildebrandt obituary) “He (Oscar Hildebrandt) went into the automobile business with his brother-in-law, Milton Muckey in 1912. He and Mr. Muckey had one of the first automobile agencies in the county. Mr. Hildebrandt was in the automobile business in Delano until 1939.”
stops.name: Hildebrandt Building

stops.title: Indigenous Peoples
stops.summary: Long before Delano was founded, the land along the Crow River was part of the homeland of the Dakota people , who had lived in relationship with the land for centuries. Their presence remains reflected in many Minnesota place names, including Minnesota itself, derived from the Dakota Mni Sota , meaning “cloudy water” or “sky-tinted water.” The Dakota moved seasonally between winter camps in protected woodlands and summer homes near water and planting grounds, hunting, gathering, gardening, and passing their history and traditions from one generation to the next. Central to Dakota life was an understanding that people were related to the earth, water, plants, animals, and sky and therefore had a responsibility to care for them. This land was not simply a place the Dakota passed through—it was their home. Delano’s later settlement and development took place only after Dakota people had been displaced from their homeland through treaties, forced removal, violence, and exile, making their history an essential first chapter in understanding the story of Delano.
stops.name: Indigenous Peoples

stops.title: Leiter Oil Company
stops.subtitle: Built 1923
stops.summary: Founded in 1912 by Frank and Oscar Leiter, the Leiter Oil Company became a longtime fixture of Delano’s automotive history and held the distinction of being the oldest independent jobber with Pure Oil. The Leiter filling station at Bridge Avenue and Highway 12 was built in 1923, and Oscar Leiter went on to operate the oil company while also becoming a prominent local automobile dealer. The business weathered repeated Crow River floods, including major flooding in 1952, 1957, and 1965, before Oscar’s son Edward sold the company in 1969. Over the years, changes in ownership and oil companies transformed the service station into Adolph’s Union 76, while the Leiter Auto Company evolved into a Ford dealership. The Leiter automotive legacy remains visible in Delano today: Absolute Automotive and Brinkman’s Trailers.
stops.name: Leiter Oil Company

stops.title: Plotnik’s Blacksmith
stops.subtitle: EST. 1889
stops.summary: For more than a century, Plotnik’s Blacksmith Shop stood as a reminder of the craftsmanship, ingenuity, and work ethic that helped build the Delano community. Founded in 1887 by Polish immigrant and blacksmith Paul Plotnik , the business grew from a small rented shop into a thriving operation producing and repairing the wagons, farm implements, tools, and equipment needed by a growing agricultural community. Paul’s son Louis joined the business, and later generations adapted the shop as horses gave way to tractors and modern machinery, creating everything from flagpoles and church crosses to custom metalwork. Although the forge eventually quieted, the Plotnik family’s long tradition of blacksmithing and community service remains an important link to Delano’s early history and the skilled trades that helped shape the town.
stops.name: Plotnik's Blacksmith

stops.title: Rieder Homestead Barn
stops.summary: The Rieder barn was built in 1881 by Andrew Rieder (1836-1911) who emigrated from Baudenbach, Bavaria, Germany in 1861. It was part of the original homestead.
stops.name: Rieder Homestead Barn

stops.title: The Drive-In
stops.subtitle: Buit 1957
stops.summary: Since opening as an A&W Drive-In in 1957 , Delano’s beloved drive-in at 115 Babcock Boulevard has been much more than a place for burgers, fries, and root beer—it has been a community gathering place where generations of young people worked, friends met, and lasting memories were made. After operating for years as the Delano Drive-In, Mike and Vickie Mirenda purchased the business in 1982 and eventually transformed it into the unmistakable pink Peppermint Twist , complete with its famous raspberry shakes and whimsical Teddy Bear Park. Remarkably, the original 1957 building remains, and the tradition continues through generations of employees—including daughters and granddaughters of some of the original carhops. Today, the Peppermint Twist remains a nostalgic Delano destination where people come not only to eat, but to play, visit, and remember summers gone by.
stops.name: The Drive-In

stops.title: Delano Central Park
stops.subtitle: EST. 1901
stops.summary: Delano Central Park has been a center of community life for more than a century. After lively public debate and a successful 1901 bond vote, land was purchased and a fenced ballpark opened in 1902. The park soon became home to Delano’s Fourth of July celebrations, baseball, tennis, dances, and community gatherings. Delano Central Park - SoCT Delano Central Park - SoCT Over the years, Central Park has endured significant flooding, including four to six feet of water in 1965, while continuing to grow through land donations and new recreational facilities. Delano Central Park - SoCT Today the park complex includes the Delano Municipal Baseball Stadium, Cramer Park, Big Rock Play Area, and a splashpad, continuing its long tradition as a place for recreation, celebrations, and community life. Delano Central Park - SoCT Delano Central Park - SoCT
stops.name: Central Park

stops.title: General Federated Women’s Club of Delano
stops.subtitle: EST. 1968
stops.summary: For more than half a century, the GFWC Delano Women’s Club has made a lasting difference in the Delano community through service, volunteerism, and generous support of local projects and organizations. Established in 1968 as part of the General Federation of Women’s Clubs, the club has helped enhance parks, trails, the library, youth programs, community events, and countless charitable causes. From launching an award-winning recycling program and helping build the Central Park gazebo to supporting local families and organizations, GFWC Delano reflects a long tradition of women working together to strengthen their community and improve the lives of others.
stops.name: General Federated Women's Club

stops.title: Delano 4th of July
stops.summary: For generations, the Fourth of July has been one of Delano’s most anticipated community celebrations. Newspaper accounts dating back to the 1880s tell of patriotic processions, bands, fire companies, speeches, picnics, contests, dancing, and other festivities that brought residents and visitors together to celebrate Independence Day. While the events, entertainment, and traditions have changed through the years, the spirit of the celebration has remained remarkably familiar—a community gathering filled with patriotism, fun, friendship, and hometown pride. These stories from Delano’s past offer a glimpse of how generations before us celebrated the Fourth and helped build a tradition is one of the oldest and biggest in Minnesota today.
stops.name: Delano 4th of July

stops.title: Delano American Legion War Memorials
stops.summary: Delano’s American Legion Memorial honors the local men who gave their lives in service to their country, preserving not only their names but the stories of the people behind them. Spanning conflicts from the Civil War and Spanish-American War through World Wars I and II and the Vietnam War, these biographies tell of young men who left their families, farms, schools, and hometown to serve. Their individual stories of courage, sacrifice, and loss ensure that Delano remembers those who served—and the profound price some paid for the freedoms enjoyed by generations that followed.
stops.name: Delano American Legion Memorial

stops.title: Delano Light the Night
stops.subtitle: est. 2020
stops.summary: Delano Light the Night is a volunteer run-nonprofit organization whose mission is to help bring joy and happiness to the community during the holiday season by decorating Central Park with a beautiful Christmas display. Delano Light the Night began in 2020 as a small memorial display created by Dorothy Zitzloff and her son Brad, in remembrance of Dorothy’s late husband/Brad’s father, Dave. What started as a family’s display of love, grew little by little each year, eventually expanding to what it is today. With over 1000 color changing pixl lights, interactive props, lighted archways, towering mega-trees, and a walking path lined by over 100 lighted trees sponsored and beautifully decorated by local families, businesses and community organizations, Delano’s Central Park transforms into a winter wonderland. The display continues to expand each year as new props and lights are added. Delano Light the Night’s display is open from Thanksgiving weekend through the end of December each year. Throughout the month, there are events and activities that happen each weekend, including Christmas caroling, musical performances, firepits for making smores, a concession stand (located in the Splashpad building) a visit from the Delano Ambassadors and even pictures with Santa. In 2025, heated clear poly Igloos were added in the splash pad area, available to rent for a Christmas meal under the lights and catered from local restaurants. In 2024, the Zitloff family decided that the display had become too much to manage for just them and the friends who had been helping them, and a decision was made to seek help from the community. Volunteers were recruited, and a committee of about 10 members was formed, headed by Dorothy and Brad. Each year, the Light the Night committee members dedicate countless hours during the “off season” to advertising and fundraising efforts, repairing props, and planning the next display. A display of this magnitude takes hundreds of man-hours to build and tear down each year. Starting each October, the DLTN committee members begin assembling the display, working in the park each weekend. Many more volunteers are recruited from local churches and community organizations to help during set-up. For more information or to help volunteer, visit DLTN’s website at: https://www.delanolightthenight.com .
stops.name: Delano Light the Night

stops.title: Delano Municipal Baseball Park
stops.subtitle: EST. 1875
stops.summary: Baseball has been part of Delano’s story almost from the community’s beginning, with its first organized club formed in 1875 —just five years after Crow River became Delano. From the early Delano Crickets and Millers to the Colts and today’s A’s, generations of players, coaches, businesses, and fans have built a proud amateur baseball tradition. Delano teams have made numerous appearances in the Minnesota State Amateur Baseball Tournament, highlighted by a 1988 state championship , while the community has hosted the tournament several times. At the heart of that tradition is Delano Municipal Stadium in Central Park, a community landmark for more than a century and one of Minnesota’s oldest ballparks. Together, the teams, players, ballpark, and generations of loyal spectators have made baseball an enduring part of Delano’s identity.
stops.name: Delano Municipal Baseball

stops.title: Delano Royalty
stops.subtitle: EST. 1968
stops.summary: The Delano Royalty Organization began in 1968 as part of The annual Delano 4th of July Celebration. It was formed by Eleanor Pagenkopt and Carol Traen. Margaret Cedergren was crowned Miss Delano and the Princesses crowned were Catherine Ditty and Joyce Gerard.
stops.name: Delano Royalty

stops.title: Delano Snowstormers
stops.subtitle: “Supporting Our Trails Since 1971”
stops.summary: Club Membership (family & individual), includes membership in the Wright County Snowmobile Association, Minnesota United Snowmobilers Association, Delano Area Chamber of Commerce, and have DNR-Certified Youth Snowmobile Safety Instructors. Snowstormers are a local non-profit snowmobile club who performs trail maintenance and development each spring and fall to establish trails to local and nearby businesses keeping links throughout the county. Groomer drivers manage grooming duties of 50 plus miles of trails with a Wright County Snowmobile Association groomer. A club warming shelter nestled in the woods along the scenic trail route provides snowmobilers the opportunity for a warm break from their ride. Snowstormers appreciate and respect landowners’ private properties as they permit use of their land for snowmobiling. The club takes pride in keeping trail systems maintained and safe for all to ride.
stops.name: Delano Snowstormers

stops.title: Delano Sportsman's Club
stops.subtitle: EST. 1898
stops.summary: Founded around 1898 as the Delano Gun Club, the Delano Sportsmen’s Club is one of Minnesota’s oldest organizations of its kind. What began as a small group focused on hunting, dog training, and trap shooting grew into an organization dedicated to conservation, wildlife habitat, outdoor education, and community service. Over the years, the club has helped protect the Crow River, improved wildlife habitat, developed public lake accesses, and offered firearm and bow hunter safety courses to generations of area residents. With expanded facilities and a membership that grew to more than 500, the Delano Sportsmen’s Club has also generously supported conservation organizations, youth programs, and charitable causes while continuing its long tradition of responsible outdoor recreation and stewardship.
stops.name: Delano Sportsman's Club
